policies.reject.policy.document_malforme: The bundle is not valid YAML. The parser said: {detail}
policies.reject.policy.schema_version_un: schema_version {found} is not supported. This server understands {supported}.
policies.reject.policy.tenant_missing: The bundle names no tenant. Add a tenant line: the tenant selects which compiled program is served.
policies.reject.policy.no_rules: The bundle has no rules. Add at least one: an empty bundle denies everything by default and says nothing about why.
policies.reject.policy.timezone_unknown: Time zone {timezone} is not a known IANA location. Use a name such as Europe/Lisbon, or leave the key out for UTC.
policies.reject.policy.label_vocabulary_: Label key {label_key} declares no values. List the values a rule may match, or remove the key.
policies.reject.policy.group_vocabulary_: The group list contains an empty name. Remove it.
policies.reject.rule.id_missing: This rule has no id. Give it one: the id is what an explanation names and what an operator searches for.
policies.reject.rule.id_duplicate: Rule id {id} is already used at line {other_line}. An id identifies its rule in every explanation and audit record, so each must be unique.
policies.reject.rule.unreachable: This rule can never match: rule {shadowed_by} at line {other_line} already matches everything it does. Narrow this rule, or move it above {shadowed_by}.
policies.reject.rule.effect_missing: This rule states no effect. Add effect: allow or effect: deny.
policies.reject.rule.deny_carries_route: A deny rule carries a route. A denied connection has no snapshot, so remove the route block or make the rule an allow.
policies.reject.rule.allow_needs_route: An allow rule carries no route. Add a route block: an allow with no snapshot is a connection with no policy.
policies.reject.rule.deny_needs_reason: A deny rule carries no reason. Add one: it is what an operator reads when they resolve the decision id.
policies.reject.match.unknown_group: Group {group} is not declared in the bundle's groups list. Declare it there, or correct the spelling.
policies.reject.match.unknown_label_key: Label key {label_key} is not declared in the bundle's labels map. Declare it there, or correct the spelling.
policies.reject.match.unknown_label_valu: Label {label_key}={label_value} is not declared in the bundle's labels map. Declare the value there, or correct the spelling.
policies.reject.match.invalid_cidr: {cidr} is not a valid address or CIDR prefix.
policies.reject.match.invalid_hostname_p: {pattern} is not a valid hostname pattern. Use an exact name, or one leading wildcard such as *.prod.example.com.
policies.reject.match.empty_term: The {axis} match declares {term} with no values. List at least one, or remove the key: an empty list matches nothing, and is almost never what was meant.
policies.reject.route.intent_missing: The route states no intent. Add intent: direct or intent: hops-permitted.
policies.reject.route.channels_missing: The route has no channels key. State the channel types: an empty list denies every one and is a policy, but leaving the key out is not.
policies.reject.route.filter_mode_missin: The route's filter policy states no mode. Add mode: whitelist or mode: blacklist: a filter with no defined default can fail open by omission.
policies.reject.route.forward_destinatio: The route permits the {channel} channel but names no forwarding destinations. Add forwards.{list}: an unconstrained forwarding axis is a mistake, not a wildcard.
policies.reject.route.subsystems_missing: The route permits subsystems but names none. List them: sftp can be denied on its own only if subsystems are named one by one.
policies.reject.route.filter_policy_both: The route's filter policy sets both a rule list and a restricted-exec allow-list. The two tiers are alternatives, never layers: keep one.
policies.reject.route.restricted_exec_em: The route sets exec_mode: restricted but names no commands, so it denies every exec. If that is the intent, say so with an empty channels or requests list instead.
policies.reject.route.invalid_destinatio: {destination} is not a valid forwarding destination. Use a host, a wildcard such as *.prod, or a CIDR prefix, with an optional port or port range.
policies.reject.route.ladder_empty: The route declares a credentials ladder with no entries. List at least one method, or remove the key to leave the proxy its own configured method.
policies.reject.route.exec_mode_mismatch: The route declares a restricted-exec allow-list, but its exec_mode is not restricted, so the list would never decide anything. Set exec_mode: restricted, or remove the list.
policies.reject.route.session_deadline_i: Session deadline {duration} is not a positive duration. Use a form such as 8h or 45m.
policies.reject.route.concurrency_invali: Concurrency cap {field} is negative. Use a positive cap, or 0 for none.
policies.reject.route.algorithm_floor_pr: The route sets algorithm floor {floor} with algorithm profile {profile}, which widens the key-exchange axis the floor narrows. A proxy refuses the pair because the leg could never connect: drop the floor, or use the default or legacy-rsa-sha1 profile.
policies.reject.route.algorithm_ban_empt: Entry {index} of algorithm_bans.{axis} is empty. Name the algorithm exactly as SSH spells it.
policies.reject.route.algorithm_ban_repe: algorithm_bans.{axis} lists {name} twice. List each identifier once: the record shows a ban exactly as it was issued.
policies.reject.cache.key_empty: The rule's cache hint names no key components, and a hint with no key is not cacheable. List what the key is derived from, or remove the hint.
policies.reject.cache.key_not_identity_b: The rule's cache key does not include subject. A key shared across identities would serve one user another user's policy.
policies.reject.cache.ttl_invalid: Cache lifetime {ttl} is not positive. A hint with no lifetime is not a hint: remove it, or give it one.
policies.reject.cache.hint_on_deny: A deny rule carries a cache hint. A proxy never reuses a denial, so the hint would never be read: remove it.
policies.reject.cache.key_component_dupl: Cache key component {component} is listed twice. Remove the duplicate.
policies.reject.credential.method_missin: Ladder entry {index} names no method. Every entry names one of the four the contract defines.
policies.reject.credential.username_miss: Ladder entry {index} ({method}) names no username. Every method requires one, and the proxy refuses the route at its first authorize call. Name the account, and never derive it from the identity's login.
policies.reject.credential.username_empt: Ladder entry {index} declares a literal username with no value. Write the account name.
policies.reject.credential.param_wrong_m: Ladder entry {index} sets {param}, which method {method} does not take. Remove it, or change the method.
policies.reject.credential.platform_miss: Ladder entry {index} is ephemeral-account and names no platform. It is never inferred: a wrong guess runs configuration commands against the wrong parser.
policies.reject.credential.credential_ki: Ladder entry {index} is ephemeral-account and names no credential_kind. Choose password or publickey: a default would hand out the weaker of two different exposures.
policies.reject.credential.expiry_postur: Ladder entry {index} is ephemeral-account and names no expiry_posture. Choose target-enforced, proxy-enforced or accepted-risk.
policies.reject.credential.lifetime_miss: Ladder entry {index} has expiry posture {posture} and no lifetime_seconds. A posture that enforces an expiry needs an expiry to enforce.
policies.reject.credential.lifetime_inva: Ladder entry {index} has lifetime_seconds {lifetime}. It must be positive.
policies.reject.credential.device_field_: Ladder entry {index} declares device field {field}. A name is 1 to {max} characters of lowercase letters, digits, hyphens and underscores.
Ladder entry {index} declares device field {field} with a value that is empty or longer than {max} characters.
Ladder entry {index} declares {count} device fields. At most {max} ride on one entry.
Ladder entry {index} declares device field {field} on method {method}. Device fields belong to ephemeral-account; anywhere else one is a typo that would be carried silently.
policies.reject.enforcement.interactive_: enforcement.execution is no-interactive-shell, but the route still permits {request}. Deny both shell and pty-req, or choose a rung the route actually stands on.
policies.reject.enforcement.permitted_re: enforcement.execution is no-interactive-shell, but the route names no requests allow-list. A request axis nobody polices permits a shell, so the claim cannot hold.
policies.reject.enforcement.restricted_e: enforcement.execution is {rung}, but the route's filter policy is not exec_mode: restricted. That rung is the restricted allow-list applied to the account, so the two must agree.
policies.reject.enforcement.platform_rol: enforcement.execution is platform-authorized, but no platform_role is named. The role is the authorization the rung claims.
A platform_role is named, but enforcement.execution is {rung}. The role belongs to platform-authorized and means nothing elsewhere.
policies.reject.enforcement.destinations: enforcement.reach is account-egress-restricted, but no permitted_destinations are named. The destination list is what the restriction is made of.
policies.reject.enforcement.attestation_: enforcement.{axis} is platform-attested but carries no attestation. Name who asserts it (asserted_by) and the evidence (reference): this system does not verify an attested rung.
An attestation is carried, but no axis is platform-attested (execution is {execution}, reach is {reach}). An applied rung is configured by the proxy and has nobody to attribute.
policies.reject.enforcement.applied_rung: enforcement.{axis} is {rung}, which the proxy applies to an account it administers, but no ladder entry creates the account. The proxy refuses that answer outright: add an ephemeral-user or ephemeral-account entry, or use platform-attested if the target already enforces it.
policies.reject.scope.name_invalid: Scope {scope} is not a usable name. A scope name is the text a grant carries and a rule matches, so it may not be blank, padded, longer than 128 characters, or contain control characters.
policies.reject.scope.privileged_fails_o: Scope {scope} is privileged and says unanswered: open. A privileged window never counts on an unconfirmed push: use closed or outage, or leave the key out.
policies.reject.obligation.kind_missing: Obligation {index} names no kind. Use record-session, require-approval or require-step-up.
policies.reject.obligation.duplicate: Obligation {obligation} is listed twice. Remove the duplicate.
policies.reject.obligation.on_deny: A deny rule carries obligation {obligation}. Obligations are things a permitted session must do, and a denied one has none.
policies.reject.bundle.tenant_mismatch: The bundle names tenant {bundle}, but it was sent to tenant {tenant}. A bundle says which tenant it serves: change its tenant line, or send it to that tenant.
policies.reject.unknown: The compiler answered {code}, which this console has no sentence for.
policies.finding.satisfiability.proxies_: No proxy in this tenant has declared what it can serve, so no rule can be judged against a build.
policies.finding.satisfiability.no_proxy: No declaring proxy can serve the route of rule {rule}. On a proxy, a rung it cannot honour is skipped silently, so the ladder gets shorter with no error anywhere. {proxies_count, plural, one {# proxy falls} other {# proxies fall}} short.
policies.finding.satisfiability.target_c: A fresh capability record says {targets_count, plural, one {# target} other {# targets}} that rule {rule} reaches cannot take the rung it claims.
policies.finding.satisfiability.target_u: The rung rule {rule} applies is not proven on {targets_count, plural, one {# target} other {# targets}}: each one's capability record is stale, undated or absent. The absence of proof is not proof of absence.
policies.finding.authoring.interpreter_i: Rule {rule}'s restricted allow-list names {executable}, an interpreter ({interpreter}) that can hand back a shell. Under rung {rung} the list is not the boundary it claims; the real guarantee is {guarantee} at best.
policies.finding.authoring.cache_hint_ou: Rule {rule} carries a {ttl_seconds}-second cache hint, but it is gated by a condition its cache key does not carry, and no grant or duration bounds the route. A proxy would reuse the answer after the condition stops holding.
policies.finding.authoring.cache_hint_sp: Rule {rule} is gated by {term} and carries a {ttl_seconds}-second cache hint. A proxy reuses a cached decision by identity, target, port, method and hop trail, never by the client's address, so the hint admits the same identity from any address.
policies.finding.algorithm.floor_undecla: Rule {rule} sets algorithm floor {floor}, which {proxies_count, plural, one {# proxy has} other {# proxies have}} not declared, so authorize refuses the route there.
policies.finding.algorithm.axis_emptied: On {proxies_count, plural, one {# build} other {# builds}}, the bans of rule {rule} leave the {axis} axis nothing to offer under profile {profile}, so authorize refuses the route there.
policies.finding.algorithm.declaration_u: {proxies_count, plural, =0 {No build has declared the algorithms it offers, so the bans of rule {rule} cannot be judged.} one {# build's declaration cannot judge the bans of rule {rule} under profile {profile}.} other {# builds' declarations cannot judge the bans of rule {rule} under profile {profile}.}}
policies.finding.algorithm.ban_unmatched: No recorded build offers {name} on the {axis} axis. A ban of a name nothing offers changes nothing, and a typo looks exactly like a working ban.
policies.finding.algorithm.target_below_: {targets_count, plural, one {# target} other {# targets}} that rule {rule} reaches negotiated below floor {floor}. Raising the floor breaks each one.
policies.finding.algorithm.target_not_re: {targets_count, plural, one {# target} other {# targets}} that rule {rule} reaches with floor {floor} reported no key exchange, or an old one, so the floor is not shown as met there.
policies.finding.algorithm.policy_unmet: Target {unmet_target} recorded that it could not meet the {unmet_axis} algorithm policy that rule {rule} names (cause: {unmet_cause}). The record is a past observation, and the device may have changed.
policies.finding.algorithm.policy_unmet_: The read of stored unmet-policy records stopped at {limit} records, so the warnings above may miss a target.
policies.finding.unknown: {source} reported {code}, which this console has no sentence for.
error.policy_invalid: The bundle does not compile, so nothing was stored or run. Validating it shows each rejection at the line it names.
error.findings_not_accepted: This activation carries warnings that have not been accepted. Accept each by its id to publish knowingly, or change the bundle.
error.policy_blocked: A registered policy validator blocks this activation.
policies.title: Policy
policies.lede: Every stored version of this tenant's policy, newest first: the one every decision is taken under, and every one before and after it. A version is never edited. Activating any of them moves the pointer, and activating an older one is a rollback.
policies.author: Author a candidate
policies.active.title: Active now
policies.active.none: No version is active, so every decision in this tenant is the default deny until one is.
policies.table.caption: Stored policy versions, newest first
policies.table.onePage: One page of the stored versions. The list continues on the next page.
policies.partial.active: The active version's details could not be read. The list below still marks which version is active.
policies.empty.title: No policy has been uploaded
policies.empty.body: Until a version is uploaded and activated, every decision in this tenant is the default deny. Author a candidate here, validate it and upload it, or apply one from a pipeline with policyctl.
policies.version.notFound.title: That is not a version
policies.version.notFound.body: {version} is not a version number. Versions are numbered from 1 and never deleted, so a link to one must name a whole number.
policies.version.missing.title: No such version
policies.version.missing.body: This tenant stores no version {version}. Versions are numbered from 1 and never deleted, so a link to one that does not exist names another tenant's, or was mistyped.
policies.partial.report: The publish-time report could not be read, so the source is shown without its findings.
policies.source.label: Policy source
policies.rejections.title: {count, plural, one {The compiler refused the bundle: # rejection} other {The compiler refused the bundle: # rejections}}
policies.rejections.lede: Nothing was stored. Each rejection is listed here with its place, and set beneath its line in the source below.
policies.report.title: Publish-time report
policies.report.lede: Checked against the fleet as it is now. Advice stops nothing. A warning stops activation until it is accepted by its id, which the activation's record names. A blocking finding stops it outright. Activation checks again.
policies.report.counts: {blocking, plural, one {# blocking} other {# blocking}} · {warning, plural, one {# warning} other {# warnings}} · {advice, plural, one {# advice} other {# advice}}
policies.report.empty.title: Nothing to report
policies.report.empty.body: Every check passed against the fleet as it is now.
policies.diff.noRules: No rule was added, removed, changed or moved, and no bundle key differs.
policies.diff.moved.note: The first rule that matches answers, so a rule that moved can change which of two rules answers a question both match.
policies.diff.label: {to} against {from}
policies.sim.title: Simulate against recorded traffic
policies.sim.lede: Replays the decisions recorded in a window against this policy. It is pure: every input is the record's own, nothing is probed and nothing changes. At most 10,000 decisions are read.
policies.sim.idle: Choose a window and replay it.
policies.sim.truncated: The window holds more decisions than one replay reads. These are the first {count}.
policies.sim.empty.title: No decisions recorded in this window
policies.sim.empty.body: Replay reads only what was recorded. Choose a wider window.
policies.sim.none.title: Nothing would change
policies.sim.none.body: Every decision replayed is answered the same way.
policies.sim.col.subject: Subject
policies.sim.unreplayable.title: {count, plural, one {# decision could not be replayed} other {# decisions could not be replayed}}
policies.sim.unreplayable.lede: Each is listed, never skipped and never replayed as a different question.
policies.activate.title: Activate {version}
policies.rollback.title: Roll back to {version}
policies.activate.body: Activating {version} makes it the policy every decision in this tenant is taken under, from the next decision on. {active}, active now, stays stored and can be activated again.
policies.activate.bodyFirst: Activating {version} makes it the policy every decision in this tenant is taken under, from the next decision on.
policies.rollback.body: {version} is older than {active}, the version active now, so activating it is a rollback. Every decision from the next on is taken under {version}. {active} stays stored and can be activated again.
policies.activate.checking: Checking the publish-time report against the fleet as it is now.
policies.activate.unread: The publish-time report could not be read first. Activation checks it again, and refuses if it must.
policies.activate.hint: The name must match exactly. Decisions taken under it are not taken back by a later rollback.
policies.activate.clear: The publish-time report holds no warning and no blocking finding.
policies.activate.blocking: {count, plural, one {A blocking finding stops this activation outright.} other {# blocking findings stop this activation outright.}}
policies.activate.warnings: {total, plural, one {One warning stops this activation until it is accepted by its id.} other {# warnings stop this activation until each is accepted by its id.}} {count, plural, =0 {Each is accepted.} one {One is not accepted yet.} other {# are not accepted yet.}} The activation's record names every id accepted.
policies.activate.done: {count, plural, =0 {{version} is active.} one {{version} is active, with # warning accepted by its id.} other {{version} is active, with # warnings accepted by their ids.}}
policies.rollback.done: {count, plural, =0 {Rolled back to {version}.} one {Rolled back to {version}, with # warning accepted by its id.} other {Rolled back to {version}, with # warnings accepted by their ids.}}
policies.activate.unchanged: {version} was already active. Nothing changed and nothing was recorded.
policies.candidate.title: Candidate
policies.candidate.lede: A source not stored yet. Validate it, see what it changes and what it would have done to recorded traffic, then upload it. Nothing here changes a decision until a stored version is activated.
policies.candidate.label: Bundle (YAML)
policies.candidate.hint: Started from {version}. Your edits are kept in this tab until it closes.
policies.candidate.hintBlank: No version is active to start from. Your edits are kept in this tab until it closes.
policies.candidate.hintDraft: Your draft, kept in this tab since you last edited it.
policies.candidate.required: Write or paste a bundle first.
policies.candidate.uploaded: Uploaded as {version}. It is stored, not active.
policies.candidate.existing: This source is already stored, as {version}.
policies.candidate.stale: The source has changed since the results below were checked.
policies.candidate.idle.title: Nothing validated yet
policies.candidate.idle.body: Validate the candidate to see each rejection at its line, or the publish-time report.
policies.candidate.changes.idle.title: Not compared yet
policies.candidate.changes.idle.body: Compare the candidate with the active version to see what it adds, removes, changes and moves.
policies.candidate.unparsed.title: Nothing to compare
policies.candidate.unparsed.body: The candidate does not parse, so there is nothing to compare. Validate it to see each rejection at its line.
inventory.title: Inventory
inventory.filter.label: Label (key=value)
inventory.filter.subject: Holder
inventory.onePage: One page of a longer list: sorting acts on these rows only.
inventory.field.list.hint: One per line, or separated by commas.
inventory.holder.subject: Identity
inventory.bindings.none: No role is bound here directly.
inventory.problem.invalid: Not a value this field accepts.
inventory.problem.ambiguous: Give a duration or an end, not both.
inventory.problem.notAfterStart: The end must come after the start.
inventory.col.subject: Identity
inventory.targets.lede: The hosts policy is about. A target's labels are policy inputs: changing one can change who is allowed.
inventory.targets.caption: Targets
inventory.targets.empty.title: No targets yet
inventory.targets.empty.body: A target is a host policy can name, by hostname, zone or label. Add one, or write them through the API.
inventory.targets.filtered.title: No target carries that label
inventory.targets.filtered.body: No target in this tenant has the label the filter names.
inventory.targets.remove.title: Remove this target?
inventory.targets.remove.body: Target {id} ({hostname}) and its labels are removed from the inventory.
inventory.targets.remove.consequence: A rule that matched it by label stops matching it. Decisions already recorded keep the labels they were taken under.
inventory.targets.detail.lede: A host policy is about, and the labels it is matched by.
inventory.targets.edit.title: Edit target
inventory.targets.missing.title: No such target
inventory.targets.missing.body: This tenant holds no target {id}. It may have been removed.
inventory.targets.activity.caption: The newest audit records about this host
inventory.targets.activity.none: Nothing has been recorded about this host yet.
inventory.targets.activity.more: The newest ten. The audit view holds the rest.
inventory.targets.activity.forbidden: Your role does not read the audit trail.
inventory.targets.partial.activity: The audit records about this host could not be read.
inventory.targets.new.title: Add a target
inventory.targets.new.lede: A host policy can name. Its labels are policy inputs from the moment it is saved.
inventory.targets.field.id.hint: Its id in this inventory. It cannot be changed later.
inventory.targets.field.method.hint: Leave empty for the method policy chooses.
inventory.subjects.lede: The people and machines policy decides about, their groups and their attributes.
inventory.subjects.caption: Identities
inventory.subjects.empty.title: No identities yet
inventory.subjects.empty.body: An identity is written when someone signs in through a connector, or added here as a local one for development and break-glass.
inventory.subjects.filtered.title: Nobody is in that group
inventory.subjects.filtered.body: No identity in this tenant is a member of {group}.
inventory.subjects.remove.title: Remove this identity?
inventory.subjects.remove.body: Identity {id}, its groups and its attributes are removed from the inventory.
inventory.subjects.remove.consequence: A federated identity is written again the next time its owner signs in. Its role bindings and grants are not removed with it.
inventory.subjects.detail.lede: Someone or something policy decides about.
inventory.subjects.edit.title: Edit identity
inventory.subjects.missing.title: No such identity
inventory.subjects.missing.body: This tenant holds no identity {id}. It may have been removed.
inventory.subjects.roles.lede: What this identity may do in this console and API. A role bound to one of its groups is listed on that group.
inventory.subjects.grants.caption: The newest grants this identity holds
inventory.subjects.grants.more: The newest ten. The grants list holds the rest.
inventory.subjects.grants.forbidden: Your role does not read grants.
inventory.subjects.partial.roles: The roles this identity holds could not be read.
inventory.subjects.partial.grants: The grants this identity holds could not be read.
inventory.subjects.new.title: Add an identity
inventory.subjects.new.lede: A local identity, for development and break-glass. People who sign in through a connector are written by the sign-in.
inventory.subjects.field.id.hint: Its id in this tenant. It cannot be changed later.
inventory.subjects.field.source.hint: local, or the connector that asserts it.
inventory.subjects.field.claims.hint: One attribute=value per line: each is a policy input.
inventory.subjects.field.breakGlass: Break-glass identity: its sign-ins are flagged in every record
inventory.groups.lede: Every group name in this tenant: on an identity, bound to a role, or recorded. A rule cannot tell where a group came from.
inventory.groups.caption: Groups
inventory.groups.empty.title: No groups yet
inventory.groups.empty.body: A group appears here once an identity is in it or a role is bound to it. Groups arrive with sign-ins through the claim mapping, or are written on an identity.
inventory.groups.detail.lede: A group policy can match on.
inventory.groups.policy: Policy matches a group by its name, from whichever source asserted it.
inventory.groups.roles.lede: What every member of this group may do in this console and API.
inventory.groups.missing.title: No such group
inventory.groups.missing.body: Nothing in this tenant names the group {id}: no identity is in it and no role is bound to it.
inventory.groups.partial.members: The group's members could not be read.
inventory.groups.partial.roles: The roles bound to this group could not be read.
inventory.roles.lede: The roles are fixed in this release. Who holds each one is per tenant: a role here confers nothing in another tenant.
inventory.roles.caption: Roles
inventory.roles.empty.title: No roles
inventory.roles.empty.body: The server named no role. That is not something this release does; the server may be misconfigured.
inventory.roles.partial.unknown: {count, plural, one {# role} other {# roles}} this console has no description for. The server is newer than this console.
inventory.roles.holders.lede: Each identity or group bound to this role in this tenant.
inventory.roles.holders.none: Nobody holds this role in this tenant.
inventory.roles.missing.title: No such role
inventory.roles.field.subject: Identity id
inventory.roles.withdraw.title: Withdraw this role?
inventory.roles.withdraw.body: {holder} no longer holds {role} in this tenant.
inventory.roles.withdraw.consequence: If it is your own, or your group's, you lose what it lets you do as soon as your session next checks.
inventory.role.integration: Asserts external access windows. Reads nothing.
inventory.role.requester: Asks the approval workflow for access for itself.
inventory.role.policyAuthor: Writes and publishes policy, and labels targets.
inventory.role.grantAdmin: Grants and revokes access, and ends sessions.
inventory.role.fleetAdmin: Enrols proxies, configures the fleet, and labels targets.
inventory.role.admin: Every permission, including identities, the certificate authority and retention.
inventory.grants.lede: Access for a while: an input policy reads, live only inside its window and until it is revoked.
inventory.grants.caption: Grants, newest first
inventory.grants.empty.title: No grants yet
inventory.grants.empty.body: A grant gives someone access for a while, through a rule that names its scope. Nothing has been granted in this tenant.
inventory.grants.filtered.title: No grant matches
inventory.grants.filtered.body: No grant in this tenant has that holder and state.
inventory.grants.missing.title: No such grant
inventory.grants.decisions.none: No decision has used this grant yet.
inventory.grants.partial.decisions: Only the newest {count, plural, one {# decision} other {# decisions}} this grant supplied are shown. The audit view holds every one.
inventory.grants.revoke.title: Revoke this grant?
inventory.grants.revoke.body: Grant {id} stops backing any decision for {subject}, and every session it backed is ended.
inventory.grants.revoked: Grant {id} revoked; {sessions, plural, =0 {no session was} one {# session was} other {# sessions were}} ended.
inventory.grants.field.revokeReason.hint: Shown to the holder, word for word, as their sessions end, and kept in the record.
inventory.grants.new.title: Grant access
inventory.grants.new.lede: Access for a while, through a rule that names the scope. With an approval workflow registered, this is a request it decides.
inventory.grants.field.scope.hint: The name a rule matches with grant.scopes.
inventory.grants.field.ref.hint: A ticket or incident, if there is one.
inventory.grants.field.reason.hint: Why, in a sentence. It is recorded with the grant.
inventory.grants.pending: The approval workflow {workflow} is deciding this as request {id}. Nothing is granted until it approves.
error.target_quarantined: This target is quarantined, and removing it would lift the quarantine. Release it first.
error.subject_directory_managed: This identity is managed by your directory. Change it there.
error.standing_denial_undelivered: In force, not yet delivered: no new access is granted under it, but ending its sessions and dropping its cached decisions could not be sent. Ask again to send them.
explain.mapping.directory: The subject's groups came from the directory {source}, through the entries this mapping scopes to it.
signIn.method.directory: Reaches only the people the directory {source} provisioned, by the claim {claim}. It creates nobody at sign-in.
inventory.standing.title: Standing denials
inventory.standing.lede.subject: A lock or the directory's deactivation denies every request this identity makes, whatever policy, grants or windows say.
inventory.standing.lede.target: A quarantine denies all new access to this target, whatever policy, grants or windows say.
inventory.standing.none.subject: No lock and no deactivation stands on this identity.
inventory.standing.none.target: No quarantine stands on this target.
inventory.standing.recordMissing.body: This identity has no record of its own: it was removed while locked, or the directory deactivated it before creating it. The denial still holds, and a lock can still be lifted.
inventory.standing.undelivered.lock: The lock on {id} is in force, not yet delivered: no new access is granted, but ending their sessions and dropping their cached decisions could not be sent.
inventory.standing.undelivered.quarantin: The quarantine on {id} is in force, not yet delivered: no new access is granted, but dropping this tenant's cached decisions could not be sent.
inventory.lock.heading: Lock
inventory.lock.title: Lock this identity?
inventory.lock.body: Every request {id} makes is denied from the moment the lock commits, whatever policy, grants or windows say. Their running sessions end and their cached decisions are dropped.
inventory.lock.breakGlass: This is a break-glass identity: locking it removes the access meant to survive everything else failing.
inventory.lock.field.reason.hint: One line, at most {limit, number} bytes, printed verbatim as their sessions end.
inventory.lock.field.reasonCode.hint: Optional. A stable code a report can group by, such as an incident's.
inventory.lock.preview.default: Left empty, they will see Control's words
inventory.lock.problem.control: One line: no line break or control character.
inventory.lock.hint: Their sessions end now, and lifting the lock later does not restore them.
inventory.lock.already: Identity {id} was already locked. Its sessions were ended again.
inventory.unlock.title: Lift this lock?
inventory.unlock.body: Requests from {id} are decided by policy again.
inventory.unlock.deactivated: Lifting the lock does not re-admit them: the directory's deactivation still denies every request, and only the directory lifts it.
inventory.unlock.hint: Lifting it restores nothing the lock ended.
inventory.unlock.none: No lock stood on {id}. Nothing changed.
inventory.deactivation.heading: Deactivated by the directory
inventory.deactivation.only: Only the directory lifts a deactivation: re-activate the person there.
inventory.quarantine.heading: Quarantine
inventory.quarantine.title: Quarantine this target?
inventory.quarantine.body: No new access to {id} ({hostname}) is granted from the moment the quarantine commits, whatever policy, grants or windows say.
inventory.quarantine.sessions: It ends no session, and it drops every cached decision in this tenant. To end the sessions already running, send a revocation:
inventory.quarantine.sessionsRunning: Sessions that were running when it was placed are not ended by it.
inventory.quarantine.field.reason.hint: Recorded with the quarantine. Nobody is shown it.
inventory.quarantine.hint: Releasing it later lifts it. It ends no session either way.
inventory.quarantine.already: Target {id} was already quarantined. Its cached decisions were dropped again.
inventory.release.title: Release this quarantine?
inventory.release.body: New access to {id} is decided by policy again.
inventory.release.hint: The access it denied is not granted after the fact.
inventory.release.none: No quarantine stood on {id}. Nothing changed.
inventory.targets.remove.quarantined: This target is quarantined. Release it first: removing it would lift the quarantine.
inventory.directory.title: Directory
inventory.directory.lede: A registered identity sync provisions this identity: its groups, attributes and login name come from the directory.
inventory.directory.noEdit: Managed by your directory: change its groups, attributes and login name there. Its lock and its roles are yours to change here.
inventory.subjects.missingRecords.title: Denied, with no record
inventory.subjects.missingRecords.lede: Identities a lock or the directory's deactivation still denies that have no record of their own: removed while locked, or deactivated by the directory before it created them.
claimMapping.lede: What a sign-in's claims and a directory's fields become: the attributes and groups policy matches on.
claimMapping.partial.connectors: The sign-in connectors could not be read.
claimMapping.stale: {count, plural, one {# directory identity is} other {# directory identities are}} still being brought onto version {version}. Until then, {count, plural, one {it keeps} other {they keep}} the groups an older version gave.
claimMapping.none: No claim mapping has been written for this tenant, so sign-ins and the directory produce no attributes and no groups.
claimMapping.directories.none: None: every group entry serves every directory
claimMapping.requireDirectories.on: On: a directory's group matches only an entry that lists its directory. Entries with no directories serve sign-ins alone.
claimMapping.requireDirectories.off: Off: a directory's group that no entry scopes to its directory matches the entry for its name with no directories.
claimMapping.entries.lede: Each entry turns a group name into a group policy matches on. One that lists directories applies to those directories' groups instead of the entry for the same name without them.
claimMapping.entries.caption: The mapping's group entries, in its document's order
claimMapping.entry.unscoped: Sign-ins, and every directory not listed for this name
claimMapping.document.label: Claim mapping, version {version}
claimMapping.connectors.lede: A connector tied to a directory reaches only the people that directory provisioned, found by the claim it names, and creates nobody. One with no tie creates an identity at its first sign-in.
claimMapping.connectors.none: This tenant has no sign-in connector.
claimMapping.connectors.caption: Sign-in connectors
claimMapping.edit.title: New version
claimMapping.edit.lede: The version you write becomes active at once, for every sign-in and every directory identity. Directory identities are brought onto it in the background.
claimMapping.edit.document.hint: YAML, schema_version 1. It is stored exactly as written.
claimMapping.rejected: {count, plural, one {The document was refused for # reason. Nothing was written.} other {The document was refused for # reasons. Nothing was written.}}
claimMapping.reject.unparseable: This is not a claim mapping this server can read.
claimMapping.reject.claim_empty: An entry must name the claim it reads.
claimMapping.reject.attribute_name: An attribute is named in lower-case letters, digits and underscores, optionally dotted.
claimMapping.reject.attribute_duplicate: This attribute is already produced by another entry. One attribute has one source.
claimMapping.reject.attribute_reserved: This attribute is set by the server and cannot come from a claim.
claimMapping.reject.group_claim: A group mapping must name the claim that carries the groups.
claimMapping.reject.group_name: A group entry names the group it reads, and the group it produces in letters, digits, dot, dash and underscore.
claimMapping.reject.group_duplicate: This group name is mapped twice without directories.
claimMapping.reject.too_large: The mapping has more entries than one version may carry.
claimMapping.reject.value_empty: An empty permitted value matches nothing and hides the entry.
claimMapping.reject.directory_name: A directory is listed by its source: lower-case letters, digits and dashes, starting with a letter or digit.
claimMapping.reject.directories_empty: An entry lists at least one directory. An entry for every directory is written without directories.
claimMapping.reject.directory_duplicate: This directory is already listed for this group name by an earlier entry. A directory is listed once for a name.
lag.notReported: This consumer's lag was not reported.
lag.failing: Delivery is failing and is retried by itself. Every record is still in the local store, which is the record: this is not an outage of Control.
lag.behind: {count, plural, one {# stream has records} other {# streams have records}} not yet confirmed: delivery is in progress.
lag.caughtUp: Caught up: every record in this tenant is confirmed.
lag.skipped.explain: {count, plural, one {# record was} other {# records were}} removed by a retention pass before this consumer confirmed them. That is not tampering: the local store is the record, and the pass's own record explains the gap.
extensions.title: Extensions
extensions.lede: Which extension points have an implementation registered, whether each started, and how far each downstream consumer of the audit store is behind in this tenant. A point with nothing registered shows what Control does instead: an extension that is not installed is not broken.
extensions.points.label: Extension points
extensions.empty.title: No extension points listed
extensions.empty.body: The server listed no extension points, which a release of Control always lists. Refresh, and if it stays empty, check that this console and the server are the same version.
extensions.partial.sinkLag: The delivery lag of the sink {provider} was not reported.
extensions.partial.archiveLag: The archive's lag was not reported.
extensions.partial.unknownPoint: This console does not know the extension point {point}.
extensions.inPlay.title: In play
extensions.inPlay.count: {registered, plural, one {# of {total} extension points has} other {# of {total} extension points have}} an implementation registered.
extensions.inPlay.none: Nothing from outside Control is registered: Control answers every point itself.
extensions.sinkLag.label: Delivery lag of {provider}
extensions.archiveLag.label: The archive's lag
extensions.running: Its Start succeeded, and it is running.
extensions.notStarted: Registered and not started: its Start failed, so Control serves without it. This is not an outage of Control.
extensions.startError.unavailable: What it depends on could not be reached, or it did not answer in time.
extensions.startError.not_found: Something it needs does not exist.
extensions.startError.conflict: It conflicts with something already in place.
extensions.startError.malformed: It answered with something that could not be read.
extensions.startError.unknown: It failed with an error of a kind this console does not know:
extensions.absent.core: Nothing is registered. Control's own path runs; a registration here would add to it.
extensions.absent.disabled: Nothing is registered. This point adds a capability Control does not claim, so it is off, and nothing is broken.
extensions.absent.unknown: This console does not know this point, so it cannot say what Control does without it.
extensions.absent.auditSink: Audit records are written to the local tamper-evident store and exported nowhere else.
extensions.absent.archiveStore: Retention deletes records when their window closes, and there is no long-term copy.
extensions.absent.grantWorkflow: An authorised administrator creates a time-boxed grant directly. A request someone raises for themselves is refused, because nothing would decide it.
extensions.absent.identitySync: Identities arrive at sign-in from the federated identity provider, and nothing is provisioned ahead of time.
extensions.absent.keyStore: Control holds its own software keys and signs with them.
extensions.absent.notifier: Notifications go to the webhook this deployment configured, and nowhere else.
extensions.absent.clusterCoordinator: Control registers its own single-node coordinator, so on a running server this point is never empty.
extensions.absent.actionHandler: No external system can ask this deployment to end a session or lock someone out. An operator still can.
extensions.absent.reportProvider: The audit view, Explain and policy simulation are the reporting available.
extensions.absent.policyValidator: The policy compiler's own checks are the whole of validation, and they always run.
extensions.absent.accessContextProvider: No external access context is consulted, and no system outside Hoplock opens a window.
reports.title: Reports
reports.lede: Every report pack registered for this tenant, and the reports each offers. Choose a period, the report's parameters and a format, and the file is generated from the audit store and saved.
reports.empty.title: No report pack is registered
reports.empty.body: Nothing that packages reports is registered with this deployment, so the audit view is the reporting available: query records by subject, target, session, kind and period, and Explain any decision. That is Control's own answer, and nothing is broken.
reports.partial.provider: The report pack {provider} could not list its reports.
reports.provider.unlisted: Its reports are not listed because it could not answer. That is not a pack with no reports.
reports.provider.none: This pack offers no report for this tenant.
reports.formats.label: Formats
reports.parameters.count: {count, plural, =0 {No parameters} one {# parameter} other {# parameters}}
reports.form.label: Generate this report
reports.period.hint: In your time zone. The start is included and the end is not.
reports.failed.broken: The report stopped before its end, so nothing was saved. A report that did not finish is never offered as one.
reports.fault.invalid: This value is not one the report accepts.
reports.fault.order: The end must be after the start.
error.report_provider_failed: The report pack failed to answer. This is an outage of the pack, not a denial.
error.report_provider_unavailable: The report pack could not be reached, or did not answer in time. This is an outage, not a denial.
error.report_generation_busy: This server is already generating as many reports as it allows at once. Try again in a moment.
